Synopsis

Growing up in poverty, Sunny never expected anything good from life. However, even he did not anticipate being chosen by the Nightmare Spell and becoming one of the Awakened - an elite group of people gifted with supernatural powers. Transported into a ruined magical world, he found himself facing against terrible monsters - and other Awakened - in a deadly battle of survival.
What's worse, the divine power he received happened to possess a small, but potentially fatal side effect...

IZYZI
2 months ago

I am currently reading LOTM (about 700 chapters in) and while I do love it, SS has a far superior writing style imo, but maybe that’s because LOTM is translated from Chinese while SS is written in English. Your complaint is a bit unfounded though because Sunny is forced to change his persona in order to trick those around him to stay alive, not at all due to bad writing on the part of the author.
Sunny is a dynamic character that does change and grow throughout the story though, which maybe you dont like because you are so used to Klein, who is a static and completely one note character that is never forced to question themselves or their tenets, and pretty much stays the same person throughout the story. Regardless, I would highly implore you to push through your resistance and read until the end of the forgotten shore arc, as you will then understand in what ways SS is on par with LOTM, as well as why having an imperfect but multi-dimensional character is a good thing.
